name: Nitisinone
route_note: oral capsules, tablets or suspension, with a protein-restricted diet
originator: Zeneca (herbicide research); clinical use pioneered by Sven Lindstedt, Gothenburg
owner: Sobi (Swedish Orphan Biovitrum); other formulations by Cycle Pharmaceuticals

discovery.by: Sven Lindstedt and colleagues, Sahlgrenska University Hospital
discovery.note: A triketone developed as an herbicide was found to inhibit HPPD in mammals and was repurposed to block toxic metabolite formation in tyrosinaemia type 1.

tagline: Herbicide-derived enzyme inhibitor that transformed hereditary tyrosinaemia type 1
summary: Nitisinone inhibits 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase, an early step in tyrosine breakdown. In hereditary tyrosinaemia type 1 it prevents formation of toxic downstream metabolites such as succinylacetone, dramatically reducing liver failure and liver cancer in children. It is also approved in Europe for alkaptonuria.
mechanism: Tyrosinaemia type 1 is caused by deficiency of fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase, the last enzyme of tyrosine catabolism. Fumarylacetoacetate and succinylacetone accumulate, damaging liver and kidneys and causing porphyria-like neurological crises.

Nitisinone blocks HPPD, upstream of the defect, so these toxic intermediates are not formed. Tyrosine levels rise, so a diet low in tyrosine and phenylalanine is needed to avoid eye and skin lesions. In alkaptonuria, the same block reduces homogentisic acid.
uses: Hereditary tyrosinaemia type 1, with dietary restriction

history.title: First patients
history.detail: Lindstedt's team in Gothenburg reports successful treatment of tyrosinaemia type 1 in the Lancet.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Orfadin approved for hereditary tyrosinaemia type 1.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Authorised in the EU for tyrosinaemia type 1.
